parts.text: A student is determining the resistance of a piece of wire. Fig. 2.1 shows the circuit she uses. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record the current I in the circuit, as shown on the ammeter in Fig. 2.2. I = ........................................................ [1] Fig. 2.2 Fig. 2.3

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student places the sliding contact C at a distance l = 20.0 cm from P . The voltmeter reading is shown in Fig. 2.3. Record the voltmeter reading in Table 2.1 for l = 20.0 cm. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student repeats the procedure using values of l = 40.0 cm, 60.0 cm, 80.0 cm and 100.0 cm. The readings are shown in Table 2.1. Complete the column headings in the table. [1] Table 2.1 l / V / 20.0 40.0 0.9 60.0 1.6 80.0 2.0 100.0 2.4

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of V / V ( y -axis) against l / cm ( x -axis). Start both axes at the origin (0, 0). [4]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
Graph:
Axes correctly labelled and right way round
Suitable scale
All plots correct to ½ small square
Good line judgement, single, thin, continuous line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ........................................................ [2]

ms.label: 2(e)(i)
ms.text:
Triangle method seen on graph
At least half of candidate’s line used

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R of each centimetre of the wire. Use the equation R = G k I , where k = 1.0 V / cm and where I is the current recorded in (a) . Include the unit. R = ........................................................ [2]

ms.label: 2(e)(ii)
ms.text:
R in range 0.040 to 0.055. No ecf allowed
Unit Ω / cm OR Ω
